residual_text_changes.before: The compensator comprises two \(3\times3\), 32-channel GELU layers and a single-channel residual head. Both operands in~\eqref{eq:compensation} are intensities, so the historical name ``dual-domain fusion'' denotes a limited post-inversion correction, not two restoration branches or direct log/intensity addition. Conditioning on both the observation and inverse-mapped estimate permits a small correction of radiometric contrast and bright-scatterer neighborhoods without asking the compensator to repeat despeckling independently. Clamping follows the residual update.
residual_text_changes.after: The compensator comprises two \(3\times3\), 32-channel GELU layers and a single-channel residual head. Both operands in~\eqref{eq:compensation} are intensities, so the historical name ``dual-domain fusion'' denotes a limited post-inversion correction, not two restoration branches or direct log/intensity addition. Conditioning on both the observation and inverse-mapped estimate permits a small correction of radiometric contrast and bright-scatterer neighborhoods without asking the compensator to repeat despeckling independently. Clamping follows the residual update, as shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:representation_ams}(a).

residual_text_changes.before: During eight adaptation epochs at a learning rate of \(10^{-6}\), the inherited Transformer encoder is frozen while the bottleneck, decoder, guidance branch, output head, and compensator remain trainable. Training masks are stochastic; one fixed mask per validation sample is reused for checkpoint selection so the validation target does not change between epochs. Inference uses the complete unmasked image. Freezing limits drift in the representation learned from controlled synthetic data while allowing output statistics to adjust. Because the target remains noisy and focused speckle may be spatially correlated, this is constrained post-adaptation rather than an independence guarantee. Fig.~\ref{fig:representation_ams} summarizes the numerical-domain and training/inference paths.
residual_text_changes.after: During eight adaptation epochs at a learning rate of \(10^{-6}\), the inherited Transformer encoder is frozen while the bottleneck, decoder, guidance branch, output head, and compensator remain trainable. Training masks are stochastic; one fixed mask per validation sample is reused for checkpoint selection so the validation target does not change between epochs. Inference uses the complete unmasked image. Freezing limits drift in the representation learned from controlled synthetic data while allowing output statistics to adjust. Because the target remains noisy and focused speckle may be spatially correlated, this is constrained post-adaptation rather than an independence guarantee. Fig.~\ref{fig:representation_ams}(b) summarizes the AMS training and unmasked inference paths.
